source.title: Effect of Collection Month, Visible Light, and Air Movement on the Attraction of Male Agriotes obscurus L. (Coleoptera: Elateridae) Click Beetles to Female Sex Pheromone

method: behavioural arena assay: single beetle in a Petri-dish arena with a cellulose granule impregnated (1% wt/wt) with a 1:1 synthetic blend of geranyl octanoate and geranyl hexanoate, or a blank granule; walking speed, distance and time moving scored
conditions: Field-collected males (wild, not lab-reared; pheromone-baited pitfall traps, Agassiz Research and Development Centre, British Columbia, 2014 and 2015; age unknown). Light experiment: white light (0.8 klux) against red light (0 lux, used as a proxy for darkness), crossed with pheromone against blank, 9 to 12 beetles per light x pheromone x collection-month combination over six days. Stimulus is a nominal loading (0.03 g of 1% granule in this trial); release rate was not measured. Nulls: the presence of visible light had no impact on any movement parameter and did not affect the response to pheromone; collection month changed activity but not the pheromone response (other experiments). source.authors: Dae-Yun Kim, Theerachart Leepasert, Michael J. Bangs, Theeraphap Chareonviriyaphap
source.title: Dose–Response Assay for Synthetic Mosquito (Diptera: Culicidae) Attractant Using a High-Throughput Screening System

method: dose-response attraction assay in a high-throughput screening system with a synthetic lure
conditions: Laboratory NIH strain (National Institute of Health, Thailand), colony maintained nearly 40 years, females 3 to 5 days old, nulliparous, mated; not wild-caught. High-Throughput Screening System (HITSS, three cylinders, 2.75 L, dark); BG-lure (lactic acid, ammonium hydrogen carbonate, hexanoic acid) at ten nominal doses from 10 g to 0.005 g; 20 females per replicate, 9 replicates per dose, 10 min; percent attraction = ((Nt - Nu)/(Nt + Nu)) x 100, 100 fully attracted, -100 fully repelled. Doses are nominal masses of lure, not measured emission. Overall mosquitoes were repelled from 1.0 g to 10.0 g (abstract). Positive control 1 g dry ice; the paper does not report the no-lure negative control. Culex: attraction began at 0.5 g (10.0%) and reached 75.9% at 0.005 g (Results 3.2.2); 10 g gave -50.2%; 1 g dry ice attracted 76.0% +/- 26.3%. The abstract gives no test statistic for the Culex optimum; the p > 0.05 in the quote refers to Ae. aegypti.
quote: Cx. quinquefasciatus showed a greater positive percent attraction (88.9%) at 0.025 g, whereas the USDA and Pu Teuy Ae. aegypti produced optimum attractant activation at 0.005 g (72.6% and 58.9%, respectively) without significant difference within species (p > 0.05).
note: Quote is the whole abstract sentence (39 words); the Culex value is its first clause, the Aedes values in the rest are filed on the next line. Species named in the quote by abbreviation; Methods give Culex quinquefasciatus. Family Culicidae, order Diptera as on main for Aedes aegypti; GBIF ACCEPTED in gbif-names.tsv. Not on main under this DOI or species+sense_chemical. Licence: MDPI page CC BY 3.0; Crossref CC BY 4.0 content-version vor. Crossref authors, volume 12, issue 4 agree with page.

source.title: Dose–Response Assay for Synthetic Mosquito (Diptera: Culicidae) Attractant Using a High-Throughput Screening System

method: dose-response attraction assay in a high-throughput screening system with a synthetic lure
conditions: Two strains: USDA, a permethrin-susceptible laboratory strain maintained over 50 years; Pu Teuy, a permethrin-resistant population collected as immatures from containers in Kanchanaburi Province, Thailand, January 2019, assays on F1 to F3 generations. High-Throughput Screening System (HITSS, three cylinders, 2.75 L, dark); BG-lure (lactic acid, ammonium hydrogen carbonate, hexanoic acid) at ten nominal doses from 10 g to 0.005 g; 20 females per replicate, 9 replicates per dose, 10 min; percent attraction = ((Nt - Nu)/(Nt + Nu)) x 100, 100 fully attracted, -100 fully repelled. Doses are nominal masses of lure, not measured emission. Overall mosquitoes were repelled from 1.0 g to 10.0 g (abstract). Positive control 1 g dry ice; the paper does not report the no-lure negative control. 10 g strongly repelled both strains (-96.3% susceptible, -100% resistant; no difference, p = 0.317); 0.05 g against 0.005 g in USDA was not significant (p = 0.287); Aedes USDA was attracted to 1 g dry ice at only 12.2%, significantly less than Culex (p = 0.002).
quote: Cx. quinquefasciatus showed a greater positive percent attraction (88.9%) at 0.025 g, whereas the USDA and Pu Teuy Ae. aegypti produced optimum attractant activation at 0.005 g (72.6% and 58.9%, respectively) without significant difference within species (p > 0.05).
note: Same whole abstract sentence as the Culex line; Aedes part is the second clause. Ae. aegypti is not defined in the quote by full name (Methods name the species). source.authors: Javier Manjarrez, Constantino Macías Garcia, Hugh Drummond
source.title: Congenital feeding response to a novel prey in a Mexican gartersnake

method: behavioural: tongue-flick and strike scoring toward prey-scented swabs, naive laboratory-born neonates
conditions: Wild-caught gravid females were housed in the laboratory and their neonates, born in captivity, were tested at 14 days old. Underwater test with swabs soaked in freshly molted crayfish, unmolted crayfish or distilled-water control, presented to each neonate in random order at 20 to 40 min intervals, up to 60 s each; tongue-flick attack score (TFAS), ln-transformed. NC (non-crayfish-eating) localities: 253 neonates from 34 clutches; C (crayfish-eating) localities: 65 neonates from 15 clutches (sample sizes of the chemosensory subset are smaller in the Results df). Swabs carry chemical cues only; no visual cue was part of the design. Population contrast: neonates from crayfish-eating (C) localities did not respond differently from control (F2,42 = 0.52, P = 0.60; filed as the next line); the relative response to control did not differ between populations (t47 = 0.53, P = 0.70).
quote: In the neonates from NC localities, ln-TFAS for soft crayfish … and hard crayfish … were 1.3 and 1.2 times higher, respectively, than for the control water (0.69 ± 0.33; F2,99 = 3.28, P = 0.04; Fig. 1).
note: Two cut marks stand for the means '(0.91 ± 0.36)' and '(0.88 ± 0.35)', which belong to the stimuli and drop no qualifier. 'Soft' is the freshly molted crayfish. Family Colubridae and order Squamata as on main for other Thamnophis rows (T. proximus, T. sirtalis); Thamnophis melanogaster is not a SYNONYM row in gbif-names.tsv. source.authors: Sara Nilsson, Johanna Sjöberg, Mats Amundin, Constanze Hartmann, Andrea Buettner, Matthias Laska
source.title: Behavioral Responses to Mammalian Blood Odor and a Blood Odor Component in Four Species of Large Carnivores

method: behavioural: counts of interactions with odorised logs presented in the enclosure
conditions: Captive animals at Kolmården Wildlife Park, Sweden (captive- or wild-born not stated). Four stimuli on spruce logs, 0.5 ml each: horse blood (domestic horse, frozen aliquots), the blood odour component trans-4,5-epoxy-(E)-2-decenal 1:100 in diethyl phthalate, iso-pentyl acetate 1:1,000 as a fruity odour, and diethyl phthalate as blank; five logs per day thrown into the outdoor enclosure; each stimulus presented five times per species in pseudo-randomised order (20 test days per species); continuous sampling of ten interaction behaviours over 3 h in the morning and 3 h in the afternoon. Stimuli are nominal dilutions, not measured air concentrations. Chi-square on counts of interactions. The abstract says no significant blood versus component difference occurred in any of the four species, but African wild dogs did differ (chi2 = 23.37, P < 0.0001), so the abstract and Results disagree for that species; the species filed here do not. Asian wild dogs: group of 12 animals (seven females, five males, 1 to 8 years old). Blood also drew more interactions than the fruity odour (chi2 = 15.02, P < 0.0001). Blood against the blood odour component: no significant difference (chi2 = 0.07, P = 0.786); fruity odour against blank: no significant difference (chi2 = 2.10, P = 0.147).
quote: A comparison between the four odor stimuli showed that the Asian wild dogs displayed a significantly higher number of interactions … when presented with the real blood odor compared to … the blank control (χ2 = 29.49, P<0.0001).
note: Two cuts: after 'interactions' (drops 'with the odorized logs', the stimulus object stated in Methods) and after 'compared to' (drops 'the fruity odor (chi2 = 15.02, P<0.0001) and', a second comparison given in conditions). The whole sentence is 47 words. Family Canidae and order Carnivora from main's docs/views/gaps/taxonomy-gbif.tsv (genus Cuon); Cuon alpinus is GBIF ACCEPTED in gbif-names.tsv. Not on main under this DOI; main has no sense_chemical row for this species. method: behavioural: counts of interactions with odorised logs presented in the enclosure
conditions: Captive animals at Kolmården Wildlife Park, Sweden (captive- or wild-born not stated). Four stimuli on spruce logs, 0.5 ml each: horse blood (domestic horse, frozen aliquots), the blood odour component trans-4,5-epoxy-(E)-2-decenal 1:100 in diethyl phthalate, iso-pentyl acetate 1:1,000 as a fruity odour, and diethyl phthalate as blank; five logs per day thrown into the outdoor enclosure; each stimulus presented five times per species in pseudo-randomised order (20 test days per species); continuous sampling of ten interaction behaviours over 3 h in the morning and 3 h in the afternoon. The abstract says no significant blood versus component difference occurred in any of the four species, but African wild dogs did differ (chi2 = 23.37, P < 0.0001), so the abstract and Results disagree for that species; the species filed here do not. South American bush dogs: group of 10 animals (five females, five males, 1 to 6 years old). Blood also drew more interactions than the fruity odour (chi2 = 35.44, P < 0.0001).
